questions.q: A file is loaded into a Lakehouse's Files section, but an analyst can't query it with SQL. Why not?
options: Files is unmanaged storage; it must be explicitly loaded into the Tables section (as a Delta table) to be SQL-queryable
SQL querying is never possible on any Lakehouse data
The file must first be converted to a Warehouse
Files can only be queried from a separate Azure subscription
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 4's Files-vs-Tables split: Files is unmanaged storage, Tables is the managed, Delta-backed, queryable layer.

questions.q: Team B, in a separate workspace, needs to query data that physically lives in Team A's Lakehouse, without copying it and without risking staleness. What should they use?
questions.explain: Shortcuts (Fabric Lesson 7) reference data in place across OneLake (or external sources) without a copy job.

questions.q: A team wants Power BI reports with the lowest possible latency and no explicit refresh schedule. Assuming the table is within size limits, what should they use?
options: A DirectQuery connection with no caching
questions.explain: Direct Lake Mode (Fabric Lesson 12) reads Delta files from OneLake directly, skipping both Import and DirectQuery round trips.

questions.q: What underlying storage do a Lakehouse and a Warehouse in the same Fabric tenant actually share?
options: The same OneLake account, storing data as Delta/Parquet
They share nothing — each has fully separate physical storage
A shared on-premises SQL Server instance
A shared Azure Blob container unrelated to OneLake
questions.explain: OneLake (Fabric Lesson 3) is the single storage layer underneath every Fabric item, tenant-wide.

questions.q: A scenario needs Spark-based transformations over semi-structured JSON files with a flexible schema. Which item should the team create?
questions.explain: Lakehouses (Fabric Lesson 4) are Spark-first and schema-flexible, unlike the strict-schema, T-SQL-first Warehouse.

questions.q: Why can a Shortcut avoid the staleness problem that a scheduled copy job would have?
options: Because it references the source data in place rather than duplicating it, so there's nothing to fall out of sync
Because it runs a copy every second automatically
Because it deletes the source data after referencing it
Because Shortcuts do not actually access real data
questions.explain: A Shortcut is a pointer to data stored elsewhere in OneLake (or an external source), not a snapshot copy.

questions.q: A Fabric Lakehouse's data is described in a scenario as 'automatically available under the same organization-wide storage layer as every other Fabric item.' What is that storage layer called?
questions.explain: OneLake is the single, tenant-wide storage layer underneath every Fabric Lakehouse and Warehouse.
